name: How do builder allowances work in a custom home bid?

mainEntity.name: What do allowances mean in a new home construction proposal, and how can they affect the final price?
mainEntity.text: What do allowances mean in a new home construction proposal, and how can they affect the final price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Allowances are budget placeholders used when a proposal includes items that have not been fully selected yet. Common examples include flooring, tile, cabinetry, plumbing fixtures, lighting, countertops, and appliances. Allowances matter because a low allowance can make a bid seem more affordable than it really is, even though the final cost will rise once actual selections are made. The best way to evaluate a custom home proposal is to compare allowance levels across bids, not just the total price. Ask what quality level the allowance assumes and whether it matches the design style you want. If you prefer luxury finishes, an underfunded allowance can create major budget gaps later. A transparent builder should explain how allowances are tracked, how overages are approved, and how upgrades are documented before ordering.
acceptedAnswer.description: Allowances are placeholder amounts for items not fully selected yet, such as flooring, cabinets, fixtures, and appliances. If your final choices cost more than the allowance, the price goes up. If they cost less, you may get a credit. Low allowances can make a bid look cheaper than it really is.
